clue.text: Make facts, time and time again, the heart of science

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information or facts
an era is a period of time
T is the standard abbreviation for time; 'again' just says it is clued a second time

indicators.note: the heart of a thing is its centre, so only the middle letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters sits at the centre

explanation.surface: A scientist accused of repeatedly making up data at the core of their research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time and time again' is not repetition for emphasis: time is clued twice, once as ERA and once as the abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate something is to produce or bring it into being, which is a plain synonym for make.

clue.text: Coming out with economy of language

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone emerging from a meeting with a few terse, carefully chosen words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' reads as a single phrase, but the first word is the raw material and the second tells you to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic writing is pithy and aphoristic, packing meaning into few words like a proverb or maxim.

clue.text: Thing jumping ahead of horse trial

indicators.note: being ahead of something means coming first, so one piece precedes the other
jumping things move about restlessly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse trial where something leaps out in front of the competing horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse trial' looks like an equestrian event, but it splits: the horse supplies the second half and trial alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal or terrible experience is often called a nightmare, so it works as a synonym for trial.

clue.text: Republican Party keeps working to make musical composition

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
a machine that is working is on
a do is an informal British word for a party or social event

explanation.surface: The Republican Party keeps busy commissioning a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican Party' reads as one American institution, but it is two pieces: the initial R and DO, with the party holding the working piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a form of instrumental music in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: In need of a drink? This malt whisky, in conclusion, is about right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: a conclusion is an ending, so only the final letters of the words are kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone wanting a drink is told a particular single malt is just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is threaded through the sentence: the first word wraps round R, and the endings of malt and whisky sit between them in the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thirsty means wanting or needing something to drink; the question mark flags the phrase as a description.

clue.text: Sleuth in a deli regularly knocked back drink

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the letters are read right to left
in places one piece inside another
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A detective in a delicatessen downing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' is drinking slang that fits the surface, but here it turns the whole assembled string round. TEC is a well-worn crossword word for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced or ice tea is a chilled tea served cold, so it is one example of a drink.

clue.text: Yielding excellent reversal in illness

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a complaint is an illness; its own two-letter middle is what gets turned round

indicators.note: the word literally announces that letters are turned round

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the figure 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A patient whose excellent progress has gone into reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The illness is COMPLAINT, which already contains AI; flip that pair and you get the answer. A1 is used as AI because the digit 1 looks like I.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliant people yield readily to others' wishes, so the two adjectives are close synonyms meaning submissive or obedient.

clue.text: When starting to request another song, he'll refuse

indicators.note: the start of each word is its first letter, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A singer who will turn down any audience request for an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb about the singer, but the definition is the noun, pronounced REF-use, meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is household rubbish or waste, the same thing Americans call trash.

clue.text: One enthralled by a simple finale of song in concert

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so this piece is held inside another

parts.note: green means naive or inexperienced
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a finale is the ending, so only the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A listener captivated by an artless final song at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In concert' looks like a live music venue, but it is the definition, meaning together. Green is used for someone naive.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is to act together in harmony, which is what parties who are agreeing do.

clue.text: Observer disheartened by hack returning to pass on material

indicators.note: losing its heart means losing its middle, so only the outside letters survive

parts.note: first and last letters only

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a nag or hack is a worn-out horse
to pass on is a euphemism for dying

explanation.surface: The Observer newspaper, demoralised by a journalist going back to pass on a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make the Observer the Sunday newspaper and hack a journalist, but hack is an old horse here, and the paper's name is just a word to trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, translucent cotton fabric, so it is one example of a material.

clue.text: Undermine writer's mate

parts.note: the writer refers to themself as I, so 'writer is' becomes I'M
a mate is one of a pair, and to mate is to pair

explanation.surface: Sabotaging an author's spouse or friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s looks possessive but is a contraction of 'is', and the writer is the setter speaking of themself as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or damage it, much as undermining weakens a thing from beneath.

clue.text: Impressive digital photograph?

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail
pic is short for picture

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke: an electronic picture would be an e-pic.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is used informally to mean grand, heroic in scale, or spectacularly good.

clue.text: Part of paint roller that's beginning to work

indicators.note: a part of something is a piece cut from within it, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A component of a paint roller that gets the decorating job going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' suggests DIY labour, but here it means a musical or written piece, whose beginning is its introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a song or piece of writing, the short informal form of introduction.

clue.text: Hercule Poirot originally confused after opening of shallow grave

indicators.note: coming after means following, so the jumble goes behind the single letter
an opening is the very start, so just the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter

indicators.note: confused things are muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, the first letter of the word

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's detective, initially baffled on discovering a shallow grave.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous detective's full name looks like one unit, but only his first name is jumbled whole and his surname gives just its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a tomb or burial chamber, a formal and literary word for a grave.

clue.text: Pretty carriage seen in race

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to fly is to rush or race along
carriage in the sense of bearing or deportment, one's air

explanation.surface: An attractive horse-drawn carriage on show at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective for the carriage but is the adverb, as in pretty good; carriage means how someone holds themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty and fairly are both adverbs of degree meaning moderately or reasonably, as in pretty good or fairly good.

clue.text: Glut of information, the source of which agent revealed externally

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: externally means on the outside, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: let on means disclosed or revealed

indicators.note: the source is where something starts, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A flood of intelligence whose origin a spy has disclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glut of information' reads as one phrase meaning data overload, but the definition is glut alone, and information supplies only its initial. A rep is a sales representative.
explanation.definitionFit: Repletion is the state of being completely full or overfilled, which is what a glut amounts to.

clue.text: Feature filled with anger regularly reveals annoyance

indicators.note: something filled with stuff holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A face contorted with rage that betrays irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' sounds abstract but is a part of the face, a standard crossword sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or annoyance at a humiliation or failure, a close synonym.

clue.text: Helping to suppress unions oddly creates havoc

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping of food

indicators.note: oddly points to odd positions, the first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: Assisting in the crushing of trade unions causes mayhem, a political warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb meaning assisting, but it is a noun, a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is utter destruction or wreckage, which is what havoc describes.

clue.text: Bassline composed for gay women

indicators.note: to compose is to put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician writing a bass part for a queer women's band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' suits the music in the surface, but here it means put together anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesbians are women attracted to other women, so the phrase is a direct plain description.

clue.text: Excuses arising from training in kinky sex with me

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: the two words taken as written, with 'with' joining them
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Someone's alibis stemming from unusual bedroom exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excuses' looks like a plural noun but is the verb, as in excuses someone from duty. PT is physical training, the old school name for gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to release them from an obligation, which is what excusing them does.

clue.text: Order instant tea to begin with

parts.note: a sec is a second, an instant

indicators.note: what begins a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Asking for instant tea as a starter in a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' and 'instant tea' look like a cafe request; instant is a noun here, a moment, and order is a religious body.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious order and a sect are both organised groups bound by shared belief or rule.

clue.text: Current filling subsequently rejected for sale

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way
a filling sits inside something, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: subsequently means later
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Stock that was later turned down being put up for sale again.
explanation.walkthrough: I for current comes from physics, where it is the symbol in Ohm's law.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is the sale of goods to the public in small quantities, so it names a kind of sale.

clue.text: Joy has first of uncles for a break

indicators.note: has ... for means one thing is taken in exchange for another

parts.note: rapture is intense joy

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the first letter
the letter taken out

explanation.surface: Delight at the uncles going first so others get a holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'has U for A': swap the A in the joy word for a U.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture is a breach or split, so the noun is a direct synonym for a break.

clue.text: Torn to pieces, as a roof may be

definitions.meaning: first meaning: harshly criticised, as by a reviewer
second meaning: covered with stone roofing tiles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Torn to pieces' suggests a storm-damaged roof, but it is the British sense of savagely criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is British slang for scathing criticism, and slated roofs are tiled with thin stone slabs.

clue.text: Flower's bottom part raised, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to listen to how words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: butt is slang for the bottom, and a tucked-up part is one lifted

explanation.surface: Describing the base of a plant that has been lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower's' looks like a possessive but is flower plus is, and the sound-alike is loose: a backside hoisted up, said quickly, becomes the yellow meadow bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild plant of meadows, so it is one example of a flower.

clue.text: Bang on about small breakfast item

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to a T means exactly, just right
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone harping on about a modest breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on' looks like the verb phrase meaning to go on and on, but it is the British adjective for precisely right, which equals 'to a T'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast, browned bread slices, is a staple served at the morning meal, so it is an example.

clue.text: Small birds get cold feet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: small game birds, plural same as singular
second meaning: to flinch or lose nerve

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures chilly little birds; the two halves are separate meanings, one noun and one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird name takes no plural ending, and the verb means to shrink back in fear or lose courage.

clue.text: Leave zero capital

parts.note: to quit is to leave
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Walking away with no money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money in the surface, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Quito is the capital city of Ecuador, high in the Andes, so it is one example.

clue.text: Slowly notice a soldier has nothing on

indicators.note: in a down-or-after reading, on means placed next, so this piece follows the rest

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
taken as written
a GI is an American soldier
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Gradually noticing that a soldier is naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has nothing on' suggests nudity, but it means O comes on after the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical tempo marking instructing performers to play at a slow, leisurely pace.

clue.text: Boxer dog I put up for sale

parts.note: a pug is a small flat-faced dog breed
taken as written
to list an item is to offer it for sale

explanation.surface: Someone advertising their boxer dog for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer dog' reads as the breed, but boxer is the definition, a fighter, and the dog is a different breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugilist is a formal or old-fashioned word for a prizefighter who fights with fists.

clue.text: Fine composer docked next to big city

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter
next to means alongside, so the pieces simply sit side by side

parts.note: Erik Satie, the French composer, without his final E
NY is New York, nicknamed the Big Apple

explanation.surface: A splendid composer whose ship has berthed near a large city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like praise for the composer but describes texture: smooth and glossy.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiny describes a fabric or surface that is smooth, delicate and lustrous, a sense of fine texture.

clue.text: Famous study acquired by the Queen is sent back

indicators.note: sent back means returned the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study room
won means gained or acquired
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A celebrated academic paper bought by the monarch is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Build the three pieces in clue order, then read the whole string backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned means widely known and celebrated, a straightforward synonym for famous.
